name: Added-lines gate (a pre-commit block for a repository whose history you do not own)
summary: a block appended after a repository's existing pre-commit layers that judges only what a commit ADDS (added lines and new paths) against the crossing lint, one identity rule and gitleaks; it reads its own gate files from HEAD so a commit cannot loosen the rule that judges it, lets lines already committed on the branch pass, re-checks the lines a merge brings in (pre-merge-commit), and fails CLOSED when a gate file is missing, unreadable or broken
requires: GNU awk, GNU grep, GNU coreutils
python3 (the lint's normalised pass; UTF-8 mode is set by the lint)
gitleaks ≥ 8.19.0 for the second block (8.30.1 pinned)
retires: the audit of every existing false positive before a gate can go on a shared repository, and the hand read of what a merge or cherry-pick brought in

name: Assert-or-die lint for operational scripts
summary: an on-touch pre-commit lint for backup, sync and probe scripts: a measured value must gate the exit code and ride the success signal — or must not be measured at all; flags sizes/counts that are only logged, WARN anywhere (comments included), heartbeats without an evidence payload, and bare `|| true` without a reason
retires: the code review that asks 'does this script's green actually mean anything?'

name: Closeout → continuity loop (session ritual)
summary: an end-of-session skill: sweep loose ends, spot-check live state, write the continuity block (what landed with commit hashes, corrections, loose ends, TOMORROW FIRST), touch the state snapshot, update the tracker, stamp every record with author/model/time from the live clock, commit scoped — so the NEXT session reconstructs today from the repository alone
requires: a repo with a continuity folder, a state snapshot and (optionally) a tracker file
the record-lint pattern to enforce the stamps
retires: the 'where did we leave off' reconstruction at the start of every session, and the trust-wait on an unstamped handoff

name: Crossing lint (two-list identity gate)
summary: a grep gate that refuses any file crossing from a private tree into a public repo, another machine or a pasted prompt when it carries a private shape (addresses, magic-DNS names, internal hostnames) or an off-repo literal (device names, people, domains, project codes); fails CLOSED when its literal list is missing
retires: the hand read of every file before it crosses, and the remembered question 'did a hostname slip into that diff?'

name: Exfil-guard (one-shot credential exfiltration tripwire)
summary: a PreToolUse hook for the Bash tool that denies a single command combining a secret path with a network egress tool (the fetch tools, nc, /dev/tcp…) — the classic one-shot credential exfiltration shape the file-read deny floor does not cover; fails OPEN on parse errors and only ever ADDS a deny
requires: a Claude Code hooks block in settings.json
retires: reading every Bash command of an agent session for the read-then-send shape

name: Generated-docs check (rendered outputs never drift from their sources)
summary: a pre-push gate for any generated artefact committed next to its source (rendered HTML, a published JSON feed, a README block regenerated from a tracker): re-run the render into a scratch copy and refuse the push when the committed output differs — with --fix to regenerate in place
retires: the remembered 'did I re-render after editing the source?' and the stale-page bug reports it produced

name: Lessons register (schema + lint, enforced or named)
summary: a JSON register of lessons learned where every row must say when it applies and WHERE it is enforced (status live, or proposed with a named landing spot — a bare TBD is not a legal row), with a linter that refuses the publish otherwise and reports the unenforced count as a visible clock
retires: the lessons-learned document nobody re-reads, and the retro that produces advice with no owner

name: PM vocabulary coach (exam-prep by correction)
summary: a passive skill that corrects a misused project-management term with ONE trailing ≤50-word block (right term · why · why yours was wrong, tagged to an exam domain), keeps a glossary of deliberate house terms it must never correct, logs each correction to an append-only file with a fixed schema, and nudges on domains that never come up
requires: a harness that loads skills passively from a standing rule in the instruction file
retires: separate study time for vocabulary the day's work already surfaces, and the nagging about house terms used on purpose

name: Record lint (provenance on added lines)
summary: a pre-commit lint over the lines a commit ADDS to session records (closing blocks, snapshot touches, a tracker stamp, decision rows): each record carries an author/model/time stamp written from the live clock, every backticked commit hash resolves, every decision row names its author — so a record that passes is trusted without a wait; all repository-specific paths are a JSON config
retires: the date-soak and the manual re-read of a session's closing records before the next session trusts them

name: Skill packager (front-matter validator + bundle builder)
summary: one script that validates every skill's front matter (name/description present, description under the harness's length cap, no XML tags, folder name = skill name) and packages each skill folder into a distributable archive — run with --check in pre-commit so a skill that would silently fail to load never lands
retires: discovering a broken skill front matter by its absence from the skill list days later

name: Web-triage isolation cell for untrusted content
summary: a fetch-only subagent (web fetch + web search, no shell, no files, no other tools) that reads every piece of untrusted external content — pages, search results, release notes, issues, forums, pasted URLs — and returns a fixed-schema digest with an INJECTION SIGNALS section; the main session never fetches or pastes raw web text
requires: a harness with subagents and per-agent tool allowlists
retires: the judgment call 'is this page safe to read into my context?' on every fetch
